extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys) handling PTAB appeals, RCEs, and judicial review
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural criteria for handling appeals to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, reopening prosecution after Board decisions (including RCE practice and 37 CFR 41.50(b) new grounds), withdrawal/dismissal of appeals, and seeking judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of 37 CFR 41.50(b) new grounds of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Board makes a new ground of rejection under 37 CFR 41.50(b), subsequent procedure depends on the appellant’s action; if appellant elects to proceed before the examiner by amending claims or submitting new evidence, prosecution is reopened; if appellant presents only arguments without amendment or evidence, jurisdiction should remain with the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant takes no action within two months after the Board’s new ground of rejection, the examiner should proceed as indicated in relevant paragraphs (I–III). Reopening prosecution before the examiner may incidentally overcome the originally affirmed rejection even though it is not open to further prosecution. If prosecution before the examiner is terminated without allowance, the file must be returned to the Board so that the original affirmance can be made final. A subsequent appeal may be filed limited to the 37 CFR 41.50(b) rejection and may not include the affirmed rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period for seeking court review lapsed — formal corrections and abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: If the period under 37 CFR 90.3 for seeking court review of a PTAB decision has expired and no court action was taken, proceedings as to the rejected claims are considered terminated; the application will be passed to issue on allowed claim(s) provided outstanding formal matters are promptly corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must correct identified formal matters within a shortened statutory period set to expire TWO MONTHS from the mailing date of the notice to avoid ABANDONMENT. Extensions may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136. Use form paragraph (e.g., ¶ 12.297) to notify applicant and identify which claims/formal matters are at issue; prosecution is otherwise closed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims brought up for action after Board reversal
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board reverses a rejection so that certain claims are now open to action on the merits (e.g., reversal of rejection of generic claims or claims to nonelected species), the examiner will take appropriate action on the claims thus brought up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should proceed to consider the application or reexamination for the claims brought up by the Board’s reversal. If the Board affirmed the examiner but entered a 41.50(b) new rejection, follow the separate procedure for handling 41.50(b) rejections (see related guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening prosecution after final Board decision (37 CFR 1.198) — amendment entry and RCE practice
rubrics_metrics.description: After a Board decision becomes final for judicial review, prosecution before the primary examiner will not be reopened except under 37 CFR 1.114 (RCE) or 37 CFR 41.50 and only with Director’s written authority and for matters not already adjudicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment filed after the Board’s decision is not entered as of right. If submitted with an RCE (37 CFR 1.114) and appropriate fee, prosecution will be reopened and the amendment entered. Exceptions to RCE practice: does not apply to utility or plant applications filed before June 8, 1995, or to design applications. If an amendment obviously places the application in condition for allowance, the primary examiner should recommend entry (with supervisory concurrence). If an amendment cannot be entered, the examiner must notify the appellant of the refusal with reasons; refusal may not be arbitrary or capricious. Use form paragraph ¶ 12.298 when entry is refused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director petitions to reopen after Board decision — allowable categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions under 37 CFR 1.198 to reopen prosecution after a Board decision (where no court action filed) are decided by the Technology Center Director; such petitions will ordinarily be granted only in limited categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The usual categories for granting a petition are: (A) Board decision indicates rejection is curable by including a disclosed limitation or removing a curable defect; (B) Board decision indicates lack of specified evidence and such evidence exists and can be offered; (C) Board decision based on a practice/rule/law/judicial precedent that has since been rescinded, repealed, or overruled. Petitions are ordinarily not entertained after filing of the Director’s brief in 35 U.S.C. 141 cases or after trial in 35 U.S.C. 145 cases. If granted in a 141 appeal, steps will be taken to request remand for PTO consideration of proposed amendments/evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of appeal and effects (including RCE treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an appellant withdraws an appeal after filing and before the Board decision, the application is considered abandoned as of the withdrawal date unless allowed claims exist. Filing an RCE in an application containing an appeal will be treated as a withdrawal of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a brief was filed and an answer mailed and appellant withdraws prior to transfer to the Board, the application returns to the examiner; if withdrawal occurs after transfer, dismissal handled by the Board. An RCE must include the appropriate fee and a submission (reply responsive to last outstanding Office action) to avoid abandonment. Filing an RCE without fee or submission in an application with no allowed claims will cause abandonment. To reopen prosecution prior to Board decision, an appellant may file an RCE accompanied by a responsive submission and fee; an appeal brief or reply brief is not a submission under 1.114 unless the RCE transmittal statement incorporates the brief by reference (see MPEP § 706.07(h)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies to new grounds or substitute examiner answers — timing to reopen prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant may request prosecution be reopened in response to a new ground of rejection in an examiner’s answer or to a substitute examiner’s answer remanding further consideration of rejection under 37 CFR 41.50(a) by filing a reply that addresses the new ground within two months from mailing of the examiner’s (or substitute examiner’s) answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A timely reply under 37 CFR 1.111 that addresses the new ground or substitute answer is the mechanism for reopening prosecution; see MPEP §§ 1207.03 and 1207.05 for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal for failure to respond to new grounds or substitute examiner’s answer
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant fails to respond to a new ground of rejection made in an examiner’s answer or to a substitute examiner’s answer within two months from mailing, the Board will sua sponte dismiss the appeal as to the claims subject to that new ground or remanded rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely response (reply brief or 37 CFR 1.111 reply) is required to avoid dismissal. A substitute examiner’s answer may itself include a new ground of rejection, which similarly must be addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal of appeal for failure to file brief (37 CFR 41.37) — consequences for claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If no brief is filed within the time prescribed by 37 CFR 41.37, the appeal stands dismissed by operation of the rule; unless appellant specifically withdraws the appeal as to rejected claims, dismissal should not be entered until the extended period (up to 5 months under 37 CFR 1.136(a)) to file the brief has expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application has no allowed claims, it will be abandoned; claims allowable only by dependency on rejected claims are treated as rejected. If allowed claims remain, the examiner should cancel rejected claims and issue the application with allowed claims only (examples provided: A–D). If formal matters remain, handle via examiner’s amendment (MPEP § 1302.04) or use form paragraph ¶ 12.209 to set a shortened period (TWO MONTHS) for correction; prosecution otherwise closed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal dismissed for failure to timely reply to notice of noncompliance (37 CFR 41.37(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal will be dismissed if an applicant fails to timely and fully reply to a notice of noncompliance under 37 CFR 41.37(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The timing consequences are similar to failure to file a brief: if no allowed claims remain, application is abandoned as of the date the reply was due. The applicant may petition to revive the application and reinstate the appeal in the usual manner; a proper reply to the notice of noncompliance must be filed before a petition will be considered on the merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review options and statutory limits (35 U.S.C. 141, 145, 306, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant dissatisfied with a final PTAB decision may appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit under 35 U.S.C. 141 (waiving the right to proceed under 35 U.S.C. 145). Reexamination/patent owner appeals, post-grant reviews, inter partes reviews, covered business method reviews, and derivation proceedings have specified judicial review paths and limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexaminations: patent owner dissatisfied may appeal only to the CAFC. Post-grant/inter partes reviews and covered business method reviews: appeal only to CAFC (35 U.S.C. 319, 329). Derivation proceedings: appeal to CAFC under 35 U.S.C. 141 or civil action under 35 U.S.C. 146 (with election rules for adverse parties). 35 U.S.C. 306 applies to reexaminations and specifies related rights. See MPEP §§ 1216 and 2683 for further particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice, service, filing, and timing requirements for judicial review (37 CFR 90.2 and 90.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of appeal, notices of election, and civil actions have specific filing, service, content, and timing requirements: file notice of appeal with the Director as provided in § 104.2, file a copy with the PTAB, comply with Federal Rules of Appellate Procedure (including service of copies and fees), and in most cases commence judicial review within 63 days of the final Board decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional requirements: appeals from IPR/post-grant/CBM/derivation must include sufficient information to allow the Director to determine whether to intervene under 35 U.S.C. 143. Time computation: timely request for rehearing resets the 63‑day period to 63 days after action on the rehearing; holidays extend deadlines per 35 U.S.C. 21(b). Extensions: Director may extend time for good cause if requested before expiration, or for excusable neglect if after expiration; extension requests filed as provided in § 104.2. Requests for extension should be served to the Office of the Solicitor to expedite handling (address guidance provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Status and limitations of application during judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: During judicial review, the administrative file of an application will not be opened to the public by the USPTO (unless otherwise publicly available). The application or reexamination is not under the jurisdiction of the examiner or the Board unless remanded by the court; amendments may be admitted only under 37 CFR 1.198.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If remanded, amendments/evidence/arguments will be entered of record for consideration by the Board or examiner as appropriate. Do not treat the file as open to examiner action during judicial review except as permitted by remand or the narrow rules for reopening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of court papers on the Director — required methods and addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: All service copies of papers filed in court proceedings in which the Director is a party must be served on the Office of the Solicitor, not on the Director or the USPTO directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable service: (A) by hand between 8:30 A.M. and 5:00 P.M. EST to Office of the Solicitor at 600 Dulany Street, Madison West Building, Room 8C43, Alexandria, VA 22314; or (B) by mail to Mail Stop 8, Office of the Solicitor, USPTO, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313-1450. The service address may include the particular attorney’s name but must not refer to the Director or USPTO in supplementation. Federal Rules (Rule 5(b) FRCP and Rule 25(b) FRAP) require service on counsel when a party is represented.
